predecessors.name: United States of America
predecessors.text: the eleven states that seceded between 20 December 1860 and 20 May 1861 (Cliopatria's 1861 shape, less western Virginia)

successors.name: United States of America
successors.text: the last Confederate shape of 1865, reoccupied by the Union armies between February and May 1865

ledger.x: February 1861: the Confederate States of America is formed at Montgomery, Alabama.
February 1861: Texas joins.
17 April 1861: Virginia secedes.
6 May 1861: Arkansas secedes.
20 May 1861: North Carolina secedes.
29 May 1861: the capital moves from Montgomery to Richmond, Virginia.
June 1861: Tennessee, the eleventh state, joins.
3 June 1861: fighting for western Virginia begins at Philippi.
July 1861: western Virginia passes to the Union.
12 July 1861: treaty with the Choctaw and Chickasaw.
1 August 1861: Confederate Arizona.
September 1861: Kentucky becomes a battleground.
October 1861: Missouri's secession ordinance.
December 1861: the Western Virginia campaign ends.
1862: residual losses between Cliopatria's 1861 and 1862 shapes that no page opened dates.
February 1862: the Confederates leave Kentucky.
February 1862: Forts Henry and Donelson open Tennessee.
March 1862: Pea Ridge secures Missouri for the Union.
26-28 March 1862: Glorieta Pass.
April 1862: Picacho Pass ends the Confederate hold north of Mesilla.
28 April 1862: New Orleans falls.
29 May 1862: Corinth abandoned.
8 July 1862: Confederate Arizona falls.
1863: East Tennessee and the Chattanooga line are lost.
1863: residual losses between Cliopatria's 1862 and 1863 shapes beyond the lands dated above.
4 July 1863: Vicksburg surrenders.
8 July 1863: the Mississippi River is cut.
10 September 1863: Little Rock falls and Arkansas shrinks to its south-west.
September 1863: the Chickamauga-Chattanooga campaign.
24-25 November 1863: Chattanooga relieved.
1864: Price's Raid.
1864: residual loss between Cliopatria's 1863 and 1864 shapes: Georgia falls from 100% to 95% by the gazetteer, the rest being the Arkansas loss above.
1 September 1864: Atlanta falls.
September-November 1864: the March to the Sea.
October 1864: Westport.
22 December 1864: Savannah.
22 December 1864: the March to the Sea ends at Savannah ('Sherman entered on December 22, 1864').
1865: residual losses between Cliopatria's 1864 and 1865 shapes beyond Georgia (Savannah, above).
17 February 1865: the Carolinas campaign takes Columbia.
17 February 1865: Columbia, South Carolina.
22 February 1865: Wilmington.
3 April 1865: the government leaves Richmond for Danville.
2-3 April 1865: Richmond falls.
10 April 1865: the government moves from Danville to Greensboro, North Carolina (infobox: 'Danville, Virginia (until April 10, 1865)'; 'Greensboro, North Carolina (until May 5, 1865)').
26 April 1865: Johnston surrenders.
26 April 1865: the Carolinas, Georgia and Florida surrender.
1865: the Confederate relation with the Indian Territory ends with the Confederacy.
26 May 1865: the Trans-Mississippi Department surrenders.
5 May 1865: the Confederate States of America ends.

wars.name: Western Theater of the American Civil War
wars.outcome: Union victory: Kentucky and Tennessee lost in 1862, New Orleans 28 April, Corinth 29 May 1862, Vicksburg and Port Hudson in July 1863, Atlanta 1 September and Savannah 22 December 1864, Columbia and Wilmington in February 1865, Johnston's surrender 26 April…

wars.name: Trans-Mississippi Theater of the American Civil War
wars.outcome: Missouri held by the Union after Pea Ridge (March 1862); Honey Springs (17 July 1863) 'to secure Indian Territory'; the Red River campaign (1864) thwarted and the Union invasions of Texas 'each of them unsuccessful'; Kirby Smith surrendered his command in…

wars.name: Western Virginia campaign
wars.outcome: Union victory: Philippi (3 June) and Rich Mountain (11 July) 1861; the Union 'would occupy the western region of Virginia for the rest of the war' and the Restored Government of Virginia (Wheeling) led to West Virginia.

wars.name: New Mexico campaign
wars.outcome: Confederate defeat: Glorieta Pass 26-28 March 1862, Stanwix Station 30 March, Picacho Pass April; the Confederates abandon Mesilla in July 1862 and the California Column holds Confederate Arizona to the end.

wars.name: Red River campaign
wars.outcome: Union failure: the Union 'tried to gain control over northwestern Louisiana, but was thwarted'.

wars.name: Price's Raid
wars.outcome: Confederate failure: the raid 'ended when Price's troops were defeated in the Battle of Westport that October'; Missouri stays Union.

wars.name: Sherman's March to the Sea
wars.outcome: Union victory: Atlanta evacuated 1 September 1864, Savannah entered 22 December 1864.

wars.name: Carolinas campaign
wars.outcome: Union victory: Columbia 17 February, Wilmington 22 February, Johnston's surrender of the Carolinas, Georgia and Florida on 26 April 1865.

wars.name: Appomattox campaign
wars.outcome: Union victory: Lee's lines broken at Petersburg, Richmond fell 2-3 April, Lee surrendered at Appomattox Court House on 9 April 1865.

certainty.note: The frontier with the Union follows the pre-war state lines (and Virginia's line); the exceptions are the contested border states (Kentucky, Missouri, western Virginia), Confederate Arizona and the Indian Territory, which are soft.
The front lines move by campaign and are approximate; the Cliopatria shapes are snapshots, and the 1862-65 shapes are dated by the ledger's captures.
